approachQuestion.prompt: A nested value represents a score sheet. Each integer contributes its value multiplied by the number of list ancestors containing it. Return the total. A root integer has weight zero. Examples: [2,[3],[]] returns 8 because 2*1+3*2=8; [[-4],5] returns -3; 7 returns 0.
constraints: A value is either a signed 32-bit integer or an ordered list of values; lists may be empty.
The input is finite, acyclic, and has no shared subobjects. There are n total integer and list objects, including the root, with 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000; maximum nesting depth is h ≤ 1000.
Do not modify the input. Indexing a list, reading a tag, and integer comparisons take constant time.
The weighted total fits signed 64-bit integers. Addition and multiplication take constant time.

options.text: For every integer, search again from the root to locate it by object identity and count its ancestors, then sum the weighted values.
options.feedback: Unique object identity makes this correct, but repeated root searches are unnecessary when depth can be carried during the first visit.

options.text: Start at depth=1 and increment at every list before visiting children.
options.feedback: The root integer 7 has weight zero, and [2] must give 2 rather than 4.

options.text: Keep one global depth counter, increment on entering lists, and never decrement when returning.
options.feedback: For [[],5], visiting the empty child would incorrectly increase the weight of its sibling 5.

options.text: Use visit(value,depth), starting with depth=0. An integer returns value*depth; a list returns the sum of visit(child,depth+1) over its children.
options.feedback: The inherited depth counts exactly the list ancestors of the current object, and each caller receives its own subtotal.

feedback.reason: Pass depth by value into each child so a completed sibling cannot alter the next sibling's weight.
details: Call visit(root,0). Integer visits multiply the payload by the depth parameter. List visits initialize a zero subtotal and add visit(child,depth+1) for each child. Depth is passed by value, so finishing one child cannot change a sibling's context.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze method-1 as described in the revealed method. Let n and h have the meanings in Q1. Use child indices and references without copying lists. Count active call frames; exclude input and returned output. There is no tail-call elimination. No hashing is used. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair among the options.

feedback.reason: One weighted addition per integer uses constant local state per nesting level.
details: Every object is handled once with constant work; depth is a word in each active frame. No separate search for ancestor counts is needed.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Nested calls remain active along a path; their storage must be counted.
“O(n²) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: Each object is processed once without rescanning or copying its descendants.
“O(h + 1) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: A shallow but wide input can still require inspecting every object.
